title: Spot-hedge-fallback-tranche-sensitivity
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to explore a tranche-based spot/reserved/dedicated hedging strategy and compute $/1M tokens by region under three workload mixes. Meant for ops + finance conversation (working draft).

Key idea (one-liner):
Divide capacity into tranches (reserved commit, spot buffer, dedicated SLA pool). Route: latency-sensitive -> dedicated/reserved; bulk/async -> spot first with graceful fallback to reserved; critical failover -> cross-region spill.

Assumptions (working):
- Regions considered: us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1.
- GPU types normalized to A100-80GB equivalent for pricing and throughput. We use a single normalized token throughput per model-class.
- Model classes and tokens/GPU-hour (tokens produced when GPU is fully saturated in steady-state inference):
  * small (7B-ish): 250,000,000 tokens / GPU-hour
  * medium (13B-ish): 120,000,000 tokens / GPU-hour
  * large (70B-ish): 30,000,000 tokens / GPU-hour
- Pricing (normalized A100-80 equiv, USD / GPU-hour):
  * us-west1: reserved $3.50, spot $1.20
  * us-east1: reserved $3.10, spot $1.05
  * eu-west1: reserved $3.80, spot $1.50
  * ap-southeast1: reserved $4.40, spot $1.60
- Effective cache hit reduces token issuance to model by hit_rate fraction; models: cache_hit ∈ {0%, 20%, 50%}. Cache hits are served from KV cache (negligible GPU).
- Latency-sensitive workload requires <150ms p95; assume 70% of that traffic must be on reserved/dedicated (can't go to spot). Bulk/async can be 100% spot-first.
- Buffering policy: if spot reclaim rate > 30% sustained -> failover to reserved pool (operational threshold).

Simple formula references:
- tokens_per_gpu_hour (T) given above
- $/1M tokens = (gpu_hour_price) / (T / 1e6)
- GPUs_needed = ceil(daily_tokens / (T * hours_per_day))
- GPU-hour burn/day = GPUs_allocated * 24 (for reserved/dedicated warm) + spot_burn_actual (spot is elastic)

Example calculations (medium model baseline, no cache):
- tokens/GPU-hr (T) = 120M
- us-west spot $/1M tokens = 1.20 / 120 = $0.0100 per 1M tokens
- us-west reserved $/1M tokens = 3.50 / 120 = $0.02917 per 1M tokens
- eu-west reserved $/1M tokens = 3.80 / 120 = $0.03167 per 1M tokens

Scenario table: 30-day steady workload variants (tokens/day) and tranche mix assumptions
- Workload sizes: base=5B tokens/day, growth=20B tokens/day, flash=75B tokens/day
- Tranche allocation rules (default hedge): reserved commit = 40% of steady baseline peak; dedicated SLA pool = capacity to cover 25% of peak latency-sensitive; spot buffer = remainder.

1) Base (5B tokens/day) - medium model, 0% cache
- GPUs equivalence needed if all on GPUs: GPUs_required = 5,000,000,000 / (120,000,000 * 24) ≈ 1.736 -> 2 GPUs if fully steady.
- Tranche targets: reserved_commit = 40%*peak -> 0.8B/day -> reserved GPUs = ceil(0.8B/(120M*24)) = 1 GPU reserved commit
  dedicated_SLA_pool covers 25% latency-sensitive = 1.25B/day -> dedicated GPUs = ceil(1.25B/(120M*24)) = 1 GPU
  spot_target = remainder ~ 2B/day -> spot nominal GPUs ~ ceil(2B/(120M*24)) = 1 GPU (elastic)
- Practical allocation: reserved 1 GPU (3.50/hr), dedicated 1 GPU (assume dedicated price = reserved + 15% premium = 4.025/hr), spot elasticity handles peaks
- Daily GPU-hour burn if reserved + dedicated kept warm: (1+1)*24 = 48 GPU-hours/day + spot usage variable (≈16.67 GPU-hours/day to cover 2B tokens -> 2B/(120M) ≈ 16.67 hrs equivalent). So spot burn ≈ 16.7 GPU-hours/day but billed hourly on demand.
- Cost/day approximate: reserved 1*24*3.50 = $84.00; dedicated 1*24*4.025 = $96.60; spot 16.7*1.20 = $20.00; total ≈ $200.6/day.
- Effective $/1M tokens = total_daily_cost / (5,000 * 1) ≈ $0.0401 per 1M tokens. (note dominated by always-on reserved/dedicated fixed cost)

2) Growth (20B tokens/day) - medium model, 20% cache
- Effective model tokens to serve = 16B/day (20B * (1-0.2))
- GPUs required fully loaded = 16B/(120M*24) ≈ 5.56 -> 6 GPUs if steady
- Tranche targets (same policy): reserved_commit = 40%*peak => 8B/day -> reserved GPUs = ceil(8B/(120M*24)) = 3 GPUs
  dedicated_SLA_pool = 25% -> 5B/day -> dedicated GPUs = 2 GPUs
  spot_target = remainder ~ 3B/day -> spot nominal GPUs = ceil(3B/(120M*24)) = 1 GPU nominal (elastic additional as needed during bursts)
- Daily GPU-hour burn: reserved+dedicated warm = (3+2)*24 = 120 GPU-hrs; spot variable to serve 3B/day -> 3B/120M = 25 GPU-hours/day. Spot recoupling might spike during bursts.
- Cost/day: reserved 3*24*3.50 = $252.00; dedicated 2*24*4.025 = $193.20; spot 25*1.20 = $30.00; total ≈ $475.2/day
- Effective $/1M tokens = 475.2 / 16000 ≈ $0.0297 per 1M tokens (note cache helps, and higher utilization improves unit economy)

3) Flash (75B tokens/day) - large short burst (1-2 days), 0% cache, 70% latency-sensitive
- Effective tokens to serve = 75B/day
- GPUs if medium model = 75B/(120M*24) ≈ 26.04 -> 27 GPUs steady
- Because 70% is latency-sensitive -> must run on reserved/dedicated: latency_tokens = 52.5B/day -> GPUs required for SLA pool = ceil(52.5B/(120M*24)) = 19 GPUs
- Hedge policy: reserved_commit kept at 40% of baseline (if baseline=20B -> 8B, but flash >> baseline). To cover flash we'd need cross-region spill + burst on spot + temporary burst-capacity buys.
- Spot alone cannot cover 19 GPU-equivalent of latency-sensitive load; must fallback to cross-region dedicated or emergency reserved expansion.
- Cost signals: spot price spikes expected under major reclaim -> effective spot price could double during flash. If spot increases to $2.4/hr, cost for burst GPUs (8 GPUs * 24 * 2.4) becomes material.

Sensitivity analysis (quick):
- For medium model, one reserved GPU contributes ~ $0.02917 /1M tokens if fully utilized. But when reserved sits warm under low utilization, its effective $/1M tokens skyrockets. So commit sizing should aim for >=60% utilization to hit target unit-econ bands.
- Spot price delta matters: doubling of spot price moves $/1M tokens by ~ (Δ price / T). At T=120M, $1/hr change => $0.00833 per 1M tokens.

Runway and commit planning (practical ops notes):
- Run 3 tranches: Reserved commit (40% baseline), Dedicated SLA pool (hot warm, 20-30% depending on latency mix), Spot buffer (elastic).
- Maintain cross-region replication of at least 10% of reserved capacity for failover (eu <-> us).
- Define a 3-tier rollback plan: spot reclaim -> increase reserved autoscaler -> spill to dedicated SLA -> degrade low-priority tail requests (drop or queue).

Operational checklist (TODOs):
- [ ] Validate normalized throughput T for each model variant using internal perf bench (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/PR-987).
- [ ] Replace price assumptions with live cloud quotes per region (action: finance).
- [ ] Simulate 72-hour flash with stochastic spot reclaim (SRE + perf team).
- [ ] Add cost-of-data-movement for cross-region spill (non-trivial for large batches).

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we treat dedicated as 'reserved but with SLA' and price it as reserved + premium? (I used +15% in the draft).
- What percent of traffic can realistically be cached for our main customers? 20% was used as a plausible mid-case; if caching is 50% the unit-econ flips dramatically.
- For 70B-class models tokens/GPU-hour is only 30M — for latency workloads this makes dedicated/reserved extremely expensive. Consider model-splitting: small/med for fast responses, large for high-quality async inference.

Appendix: quick reference $/1M token lookup (medium, T=120M):
- us-west spot: $0.0100 /1M
- us-west reserved: $0.02917 /1M
- us-east spot: 1.05/120 = $0.00875 /1M
- us-east reserved: 3.10/120 = $0.02583 /1M
- eu-west spot: 1.50/120 = $0.0125 /1M
- eu-west reserved: 3.80/120 = $0.03167 /1M
- ap-southeast spot: 1.60/120 = $0.01333 /1M
- ap-southeast reserved: 4.40/120 = $0.03667 /1M

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally a compact, calculation-first working sheet. If we want a canonical spreadsheet for finance + ops I can convert the scenarios into per-hour rows and add an interactive parameter table (w/ sliders for cache, spot price shock, latency fraction).
